details: Global stock markets, particularly the technology and chip sectors, experienced a downturn on Friday due, in part, to concerns surrounding higher interest rates and the significant debt financing underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Following stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data earlier in the week, traders increased their bets on additional interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, prompting a shift by investors towards safer assets like government bonds. This broader "risk-off" sentiment in traditional markets typically extends to cryptocurrencies.
title: Global Stocks Drop on AI Debt Concerns and Rate Hike Fears

details: Payments modernization company Marqeta and leading cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase have announced a collaboration to enable stablecoin-backed card payments. This partnership will allow Marqeta's customers to offer cards that convert users' stablecoin holdings into fiat currency for everyday spending. Coinbase will manage the stablecoin custody, fiat conversion, and facilitate fast, low-cost settlement on its Base blockchain, aiming to enhance the real-world utility and adoption of stablecoins.
title: Marqeta and Coinbase Partner for Stablecoin-Backed Card Payments

details: Cryptocurrency markets witnessed substantial volatility, resulting in total liquidations exceeding $830 million across all digital assets within a 24-hour period as of October 16. Long-position liquidations were particularly dominant, especially after Bitcoin briefly dipped below the $80,000 mark before staging a rebound to near $82,000. This significant wave of liquidations underscores the impact of ongoing macroeconomic pressures and the elevated leverage present in the crypto market.
title: Over $830 Million in Crypto Liquidations Amid Market Volatility
